chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his sermon: 'Shall I inform you of the best moral qualities of the world and the Hereafter? It is pardoning the one who oppressed you, and maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and doing good to the one who did wrong to you, and giving to the one who deprived you.'
ai.seo_question: What are the best moral qualities for success in this world and the Hereafter according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this sermon highlights the Prophet’s emphasis on *al-‘afw* (pardon) and *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) as the pinnacle of moral character, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethics as the means to purify the soul and emulate the Ahl al-Bayt. These four reciprocal virtues transform social friction into spiritual elevation, reflecting the Quranic principle of repelling evil with good to achieve closeness to God.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said in his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> inform you with the best moral of the world and the Hereafter? (it is) the pardoning the one who oppressed you, and maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and the (doing of) favours to the one who offended you, and giving to the one who deprived you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah said in a sermon, ‘Should I tell you what is the best faculty of creatures of this world and of the next world? It is forgiveness for those who do injustice to you, to establish good relations with those who ignore you, to do favors to those who harm you and to give to those who deprive you.’”
